# `unitext` — specification

## Maturity

**Grade:** 3 · S3 E2 A3 H1 P3 · limited by scope (core), audit (no mutation run recorded), performance (not measured) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** core — CPython `str` + `unicodedata`, Rust std (`str::to_lowercase`, `to_uppercase`) + `unicode-normalization`, Go `golang.org/x/text` (`unicode/norm`, `cases`, `runes`), ICU (surveyed 2026-11-09 from their documentation, not by reading their source; CPython and Rust were then RUN over the module's inputs, see Anchoring). What a pandas / polars string column user needs is here; what a Go or ICU user also expects and is missing (language-tailored case, word-boundary titlecase, `unicodedata.name`/`numeric`, segmentation) is under Backlog with reasons.

**Audit:** review 2026-11-09 · mutation none · src ?

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-11-09 (300,000 runs clean in ReleaseSafe after the UR-1 fix, `UNITEXT_FUZZ`, 15 s; the harness is described under Anchoring; no planted-mutant check yet, see Open) · ct n/a — no secret: the module transforms caller-supplied text · panic 2026-11-09 (independent sweep of every pub entry point, `src/unit_test.zig` "sweep: …": per-code-point functions clamp any `u21` (surrogates, above U+10FFFF) to the default record before indexing; every string form decodes through `utf8.step`, whose reads are guarded by `i + k >= s.len`; the 256-byte emitter block is checked before each append; `ListOut` checks `bytes.len > cap - len` with `len <= cap` by construction; the normalization working buffer is capped by `max_segment` and the output by `max_output`, zero caps give `error.TooLarge` or an empty result; sort and compose are linear or n log n, Final_Sigma look-ahead crosses each case-ignorable run at most once; no finding, no `unreachable`/`assert` on a caller value)

**Performance:** not measured

**Downstream consumer:** no

**Where we are ahead:** a Zig implementation of all of it with no dependency; one explicit policy for ill-formed bytes shared by every function (CPython and Rust take a `str` and cannot receive them); allocation caps on every allocating form (CPython and Rust have none); `unaccent` with `ł ø đ ħ ŧ ı` and the ligatures in one call (Go and ICU need the transform chain, CPython has nothing) · **Where we are behind:** no language-tailored case (Turkish dotted I, Lithuanian), no word-boundary titlecase (polars `to_titlecase`, Go `cases.Title`), no streaming normalizer object (`Reader`/`Writer`; the writer forms stream the output but read the whole input slice), no `unicodedata.name`/`numeric`/`decomposition` (→ Backlog).

## What this module is, and what it is not

Unicode algorithms that operate on one UTF-8 string and need the Unicode Character Database: case mapping, normalization, accent folding and the `str.is*` classification. The tables are Unicode 18.0.0 (`unicode_version`), generated, with no runtime file access and no allocation in a lookup. It exists because pandas (Python `str`) and polars (Rust `str`) do Unicode case mapping by default, so a Zig dataframe that does only ASCII gives different answers on real text, and because nothing in zig-libs had case *mapping* or *normalization* (`regex` holds simple case-fold orbits for `(?i)`, `validate` the sets of code points that change under lower/upper; neither can map).

Not here: collation (UCA, sort keys), grapheme / word / sentence segmentation, bidi, IDNA / UTS #46, East Asian width, confusables, Unicode names, language-tailored case rules — all under Backlog or "What is deliberately not done".

## Wire format / algorithm

**Decoding.** UTF-8 is read with Unicode 18 Table 3-7; an ill-formed stretch is split into maximal subparts (§3.9). `Options.invalid_utf8`: `.reject` returns `error.InvalidUtf8` (output already written stays in the writer); `.replace` writes U+FFFD per maximal subpart; `.pass_through` copies the bad bytes and treats them as an uncased, non-ignorable, combining-class-0 unit that ends any normalization segment.

**Case mapping** (`case.zig`). Per code point: the simple mapping of UnicodeData (fields 12-14; titlecase falls back to uppercase) overridden by the unconditional entries of SpecialCasing.txt that differ from it (ß → SS / Ss, ŉ → ʼN, İ → i + U+0307, ǰ, ΐ, ΰ, the FB00-FB17 ligatures, the Greek iota-subscript forms; 103 uppercase, 49 titlecase, 1 lowercase entry; 18.0 added U+1DF95 LIGATURE LONG S WITH DESCENDER S → SS / Ss); folding is CaseFolding.txt C + S (simple) and C + F (full). Context: **Final_Sigma** (§3.13) for `lower`, `title`, `capitalize`, `swapcase` (and Σ reached by them): Σ becomes ς when the previous non-Case_Ignorable code point is Cased and the next non-Case_Ignorable one is not; the previous side is tracked while scanning, the next side by a look-ahead that skips Case_Ignorable code points (linear overall: a run of ignorables is crossed by at most one Σ before it). No other conditional entry is applied (Turkic `tr`/`az`, Lithuanian `lt`).

- `title`: CPython's rule: the first Cased code point after a non-Cased one is titlecased (full), every other lowercased, "Cased" being the Cased property; so `they're` → `They'Re` and `ǆungla` → `ǅungla`.
- `capitalize`: first code point titlecased (full: `ß` → `Ss`, `ǆ` → `ǅ`), the rest lowercased (3.8+ CPython).
- `swapcase`: Uppercase-property code points lowercased (full, with Final_Sigma), Lowercase-property ones uppercased (full), everything else unchanged (so `ǅ` stays).
- `casefold`: full folding; for caseless matching, not display.

**Normalization** (`norm.zig`, UAX #15). Decompose each code point (Hangul syllables arithmetically, the rest from the table of full recursive canonical / compatibility decompositions), cut the text into segments at every starter whose NFC_QC is Yes, stably sort each run of non-starters by Canonical_Combining_Class (insertion sort up to 16 marks, `std.sort.block` beyond), and for NFC / NFKC compose in place with the UAX #15 algorithm (blocked-by-intervening-class rule; Hangul L+V, LV+T algorithmically; the 961 primary composites, the Full_Composition_Exclusion ones left out by the generator). `quickCheck` is the NFC_QC / NFKC_QC / NFD_QC / NFKD_QC walk with the canonical-order check; `isNormalized` answers from it when it can and otherwise normalizes segment by segment and compares with the input without building the output. ASCII runs are copied without a lookup (the last ASCII byte before a non-ASCII one is kept in the segment, since `e` + U+0301 composes; a comptime check proves no composition pair ends in ASCII).

**`unaccent`.** NFD; drop code points of General_Category Mn; map the letters of `unaccent_letters` to ASCII; with `expand_ligatures` (default **on**: PostgreSQL's `unaccent` and ICU's Latin-ASCII do it, sklearn's `strip_accents` does not) expand `unaccent_expansions`; NFC. The two lists are derived by the generator from the UCD *names*, never copied from another project's rules file. A name `LATIN SMALL|CAPITAL LETTER|LIGATURE <base> [WITH <modifiers>]`, or a small capital `LATIN LETTER SMALL CAPITAL <base> …` / `LATIN SMALL CAPITAL LETTER <base> …` (which folds to the capital letter, as Latin-ASCII does), of a code point with no canonical decomposition is read as its base: the modifiers (hook, stroke, bar, tail, flourish …) are dropped as NFD + dropping marks drops an accent, unless they name a second `LETTER` (UR-1). `unaccent_letters` (329 entries; 304 in 17.0.0) = a base that is one letter A-Z (ð ø đ ħ ł ŧ ŀ ɓ ƒ …, ᴀ ɢ ʀ …) or one of the named one-letter bases `NAMED_LETTERS`: DOTLESS I, DOTLESS J, ETH, LONG S (ſ → s), the letters of their own alphabet's order whose ASCII stand-in is fixed by orthography or transliteration practice — ENG (ŋ → n), KRA (ĸ → q, the Greenlandic 1973 reform), OPEN E, IOTA, U BAR, AFRICAN D, SCRIPT G — and the glyph variants BROKEN L, INSULAR D / F / T, MIDDLE-WELSH V, BARRED B. `unaccent_expansions` (69 code points, 67 in 17.0.0, under `expand_ligatures`) = the named several-letter bases `NAMED_EXPANSIONS`: AE, OE, IJ, SHARP S, THORN, TH, FF, FI, FL, FFI, FFL, ST, LONG S T, the medievalist and Americanist ligature letters AA AO AU AV AY OO VY UE HV OI MIDDLE-WELSH LL, the IPA digraphs DB QP DZ TS LS LZ (`… DIGRAPH`), plus the twelve digraphs Ǆ ǅ ǆ Ǉ ǈ ǉ Ǌ ǋ ǌ Ǳ ǲ ǳ by exact name (`NAMED_DIGRAPHS`); capitals expand to capitals, titlecase to titlecase: Æ → AE, ǅ → Dz, Ꜳ → AA, ɶ → OE. Every list is checked against ICU's Latin-ASCII (Anchoring). Marks of **every** script that are Mn are removed (Hebrew points, Arabic harakat, Devanagari signs of category Mn), not only Latin accents; compatibility mappings are not applied.

**Classification.** CPython's definitions, from the tables: `isAlpha` = category Lm Lt Lu Ll Lo; `isAlphabetic` / `isAlphabeticCp` = the Alphabetic derived property of `DerivedCoreProperties.txt` (L + Nl + Other_Alphabetic, so many combining vowel signs of category Mc / Mn count; Rust `char::is_alphabetic`, polars `cs.alpha()`; NOT Python's `isalpha`; checked for every code point against the file's ranges, `src/testdata/alphabetic_ranges.txt`); `isDecimal` = Numeric_Type Decimal; `isDigit` = Decimal or Digit; `isNumeric` = any Numeric_Type (this includes the CJK numerals such as 三, because `DerivedNumericType.txt` includes the Unihan values, as CPython does); `isAlnum` = any of the four; `isSpace` = Bidi_Class WS, B, S or category Zs; `isPrintable` = not Cc Cf Cs Co Cn Zl Zp and of Zs only the ASCII space; `isUpper` / `isLower` / `isTitle` as CPython's loops over the Uppercase / Lowercase properties and Lt. Empty string: false for all but `isPrintable` and `isAscii`. An ill-formed stretch counts as U+FFFD under `.replace` and `.pass_through`.

**Tables** (`tables.zig`, `tools/ucd_gen/gen.py`). Every per-code-point table is three-stage (`vals[leaf[(t2[(t1[cp>>(a+b)]<<b)|((cp>>a)&mb)]<<a)|(cp&ma)]]`, shifts chosen per table by size): `gcflags` 23.2 KB (category, Uppercase / Lowercase / Cased / Case_Ignorable / space / Alphabetic, Numeric_Type; the Alphabetic bit cost 132 B), `norm` 12.0 KB (ccc, quick-check values), `decomp` 50.7 KB + 25.7 KB pool + `compose_pairs` 11.5 KB, `lower` / `upper` / `title` / `fold` 3.7-4.1 KB each + the `special_*` lists (about 5 KB), `unaccent_*` about 3 KB. A `look` above U+10FFFF reads U+10FFFF (a noncharacter), so a `u21` argument cannot index out of range.

## Limits and refusals

- `Options.max_output` (default 1 GiB) caps an allocating result in bytes: `error.TooLarge` (the cap is checked before each append, so a hostile input cannot make the module allocate more than the cap plus one block). Case mapping grows UTF-8 text by at most 3x, NFKD of U+FDFA by 11x. Pinned by `unit_test.zig` "caps …" and the fuzz harness (a cap of exactly the result length succeeds, one byte less is `TooLarge`).
- `Options.max_segment` (default 16,777,216 code points = 64 MiB of working buffer) caps one normalization segment: a starter followed by that many marks is `error.TooLarge`; real text has segments of a few code points. CPython and Rust have no such cap. Stream-Safe Text Format is not enforced.
- Writer forms stream and ignore `max_output`; a failing writer is `error.WriteFailed` at any size (fuzzed with every capacity of the lowercase output).
- No consumer-reachable panic: every pub function is total on any bytes and any `u21`; the only assertions are comptime (GeneralCategory count equals the table's, no composition pair ends in ASCII, unaccent expansions never longer than their source, which the in-place filter relies on).
- Thread safety: no global state; every function is reentrant.

## Performance

Not measured (no bench). Size, ReleaseSmall, stripped, single-threaded, `std.heap.page_allocator`, a program that reads one argument and prints the result: baseline (copy the argument) 120,632 B; calling only `lower` 149,912 B (+29,280 B); calling only `normalize` (NFKC) 226,560 B (+105,928 B). Unused tables are not linked (Zig compiles only what is referenced).

The CPython comparison covers the tables where 16.0.0, 17.0.0 and 18.0.0 all agree; the code points left out (17,833 with their decomposition / mapping closures: 4,815 changed in 17.0, 13,016 more in 18.0) are covered by Unicode's test and, for lower / upper, by Rust up to 17.0. **What 18.0.0 changed** (UCD 17.0.0 vs 18.0.0, per code point over every record the tables read): 13,016 code points, of which 13,007 newly assigned and 9 old ones — U+0277 ɷ, U+027C ɼ, U+AB4B ꭋ, U+AB4C ꭌ gained uppercase mappings to the new capitals U+A7DD, U+A7E2, U+AB6C, U+AB6D; U+1B3A, U+1B3C, U+1B42 (Balinese vowel signs) Bidi_Class NSM → L (not read by any answer but `isSpace`'s WS/B/S test); U+32403, U+324DF Numeric_Type None → Numeric (Unihan values, `isNumeric`). Case mappings: 41 code points (those 4, the 4 new capitals, U+1DF95 and 32 new Latin Extended-G letters in 16 case pairs); case folding: 21 (the capitals of those pairs, and U+1DF95 → U+00DF simple / `ss` full). Anchors for them: NormalizationTest.txt 18.0.0 for normalization; nothing foreign for case and classification (CPython is 16.0, Rust 17.0) — they are pinned only by the generator reading the UCD files (`gen.py -check`) and the per-code-point property test against `alphabetic_ranges.txt`. `unaccent`: 18.0 adds 25 letters and 2 expansions by the same name rules (Latin Extended-G and a Latin Extended-D capital, e.g. U+1DF72 O WITH CURL → O, U+1DF2E DZ DIGRAPH WITH PALATAL HOOK → dz); Latin-ASCII (Unicode 17) does not know them, the oracle reports them as `not-in-oracle` (163 code points new in the Latin blocks, the rest of the classes unchanged). Everything in `vectors_test.zig` is replayed in the ordinary test lane (about 20 s in Debug). Not anchored by a foreign oracle (pinned by examples and properties only): `unaccent` on strings (its lists are anchored per code point above, the steps NFD / NFC by Unicode's test), `title` word runs beyond CPython's rule (anchored: CPython's), the invalid-UTF-8 policies (Unicode §3.9 and the same boundaries as `std.unicode`, tested exhaustively on short strings in `utf8.zig`), the caps, the writer forms. The fuzz harness (`fuzz_test.zig`, `UNITEXT_FUZZ=<runs>[,<seed>]`) checks the algebra of the four forms (NFC∘NFD = NFC …, idempotence, `isNormalized` ⇔ unchanged), the three policies, the caps at the exact boundary and writer failure at every capacity; 860,000 seeds clean, ReleaseSafe, 2026-11-09 (reach: ill-formed 58 %, greek 15 %, marks 7 %, expanding 4 %, too-large 35 %, short-writer 18 %). It has no independent value oracle; values come from the vectors.

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

## What is deliberately not done

- **Language-tailored case mapping** (Turkish / Azeri dotted and dotless I, Lithuanian dot retention; SpecialCasing's conditional entries; Go `cases.Lower(language.Turkish)`, ICU locale `CaseMap`). *Not now.* CPython, Rust and polars/pandas do not apply them either (their `lower` is locale-independent), so a pandas / polars user sees none; adding a `locale` option later is a table of 9 conditional entries and three contexts (After_I, Before_Dot, More_Above). No consumer has asked.
- **Word-boundary titlecase** (polars `str.to_titlecase`, Go `cases.Title`, ICU titlecase with a word `BreakIterator`). *Not now.* It needs UAX #29 word-break tables, which exist only inside `regex`; polars' exact boundary rule could not be verified here (polars is not installed), so no vectors could be produced. `title` is CPython's. See Backlog.
- **`unicodedata.name` / `lookup`.** *Never* in this module: the name table is over 1 MB of text, against a module whose point is a small table set; a consumer that needs names reads the UCD.
- **Collation (UCA), IDNA / UTS #46, confusables, East Asian width, bidi.** *Not now / never* by module: none is a method of Python `str`, Rust `str` or a pandas / polars string column; each is a module of its own with its own data (`NFKC_Casefold` for IDNA / identifiers is already in `DerivedNormalizationProps.txt`).
- **A streaming normalizer object** (Go `norm.Reader` / `Writer`, Rust's iterator adaptors). *Not now:* the writer forms stream the output; the input must be one slice. A segment-at-a-time reader would let a caller normalize an unbounded file with constant memory.
- **`unaccent` where ICU's Latin-ASCII folds and this module does not** (`tools/latin_ascii_diff.py` names each case and fails when one appears unnamed). *Never*, by design: (a) compatibility forms — the 52 fullwidth Latin letters (Ａ → A), ŉ U+0149 (Latin-ASCII `'n`) and U+1DF95 LIGATURE LONG S WITH DESCENDER S (18.0, `<compat>` ß; a ligature `WITH` a second letter is not a letter with a mark): `unaccent` applies no compatibility mappings (use NFKC first); (b) non-letters — punctuation, symbols, fractions, Roman numerals, NO-BREAK SPACE, SOFT HYPHEN (« → `<<`, © → `(C)`, ½ → ` 1/2`): out of scope for an accent fold; (c) letters where Latin-ASCII is arbitrary: ɧ U+0267 HENG WITH HOOK (folded to h while HENG U+A727 itself is left alone; an IPA sound of its own), and the medieval abbreviation letters ꝱ ꝲ ꝳ ꝴ ꝵ ꝷ (DUM LUM MUM NUM RUM TUM) and ꝶ (SMALL CAPITAL RUM), which stand for a syllable: one letter loses it, and the syllable is a guess. The context rule of Latin-ASCII that writes `Ae` / `Oe` / `Th` for a capital ligature before a lowercase letter is not followed: `unaccent` maps per code point (`Œuvre` → `OEuvre`, see Review).
- **Stream-Safe Text Format enforcement** (UAX #15 Annex 15). *Not now:* `max_segment` bounds the cost instead.

## Backlog / deferred

- `unicodedata.decimal` / `digit` / `numeric` **values** (the numeric value of ½ is 0.5, of 三 is 3): the table is about 1,000 entries; `isNumeric` etc. exist, the value does not.
- `unicodedata.decomposition(cp)` (the raw mapping string with its `<tag>`), `bidirectional`, `mirrored`, `east_asian_width`: single-property lookups the generator can emit when a consumer needs one.
- Locale option for `lower` / `upper` / `title` (see above); `title` with word boundaries (polars, Go): the boundary tables come from `regex` (Word_Break) and should be moved here or into a `segmentation` module rather than copied.
- **Dedupe with other modules:** `regex`'s General_Category / Script tables (`unicode_tables.zig`) and its simple case-fold orbits (`casefold.zig`), and `validate`'s `case_tables.zig` (the code points that change under lower / upper), could be derived from this module's tables (`gcflags`, `fold`, `lower` / `upper`) instead of being generated three times. Do not do it in the wave that added this module; both have their own generators and goldens.
- A bench against Rust `str::to_lowercase` and `unicode-normalization` (not written: `Performance` stays "not measured"); a `size` knob to leave out the compatibility decompositions (about 40 % of the decomposition tables) for a consumer that only needs NFC / NFD.
- A segment-at-a-time normalizing reader (above).

## Review 2026-11-09 (independent second reader, wave UA)

Read in full: every non-test file of `src/` and `tools/ucd_gen/gen.py`; checked against the UCD 17.0.0 files themselves (fetched into the gitignored `tools/ucd_gen/data/`, `gen.py -check` clean before and after).

- **UR-1 (MED, fixed).** `unaccent` folded the titlecase digraphs U+01C5 Dž, U+01C8 Lj, U+01CB Nj, U+01F2 Dz to a single ASCII letter (`D`, `L`, `N`, `D`), dropping the second letter: the name rule `LATIN CAPITAL LETTER <X> WITH …` matched `LATIN CAPITAL LETTER D WITH SMALL LETTER Z WITH CARON`, which is a digraph with only a compatibility decomposition, not a letter with a diacritic. Their all-capital and all-small siblings (DŽ, dž) were already left alone, so the result was also inconsistent. Fix: the generator rejects a remainder that contains another ` LETTER ` word (`gen.py`; 242 -> 238 letters, tables regenerated, exactly the four entries gone). Test `unaccent: titlecase digraphs keep both letters (UR-1)`; seen failing with the four entries put back. Not expanded to `Dz`/`Lj`/`Nj` at the time (a new behaviour, left for the owner). **Follow-up 2026-11-10 (owner decision: parity with Latin-ASCII):** all twelve digraph code points (U+01C4-01CC, U+01F1-01F3) are now `unaccent_expansions` (DZ Dz dz, LJ Lj lj, NJ Nj nj, DZ Dz dz) under `expand_ligatures`; the UR-1 test now expects `DzLjNjDz` and a second test pins all twelve (generator: `NAMED_DIGRAPHS`, matched by exact UCD name; 29 expansions).
- Checked and clean: Final_Sigma (context tracking over Case_Ignorable, İ, raw/ill-formed units, linear look-ahead); the `title`/`capitalize`/`swapcase` loops against CPython's; the three invalid-UTF-8 policies and maximal subparts (overlong, surrogates, > U+10FFFF, truncated); the segment cut at `ccc = 0 and NFC_QC = Yes` — verified on the UCD data that NFC_QC=Maybe and NFKC_QC=Maybe are the same set, that every second element of a primary composite is Maybe, that no composition pair has a non-starter first or composite and that no decomposition contains a precomposed Hangul syllable (the segment loop does not decompose pool entries again), so the same cut is right for NFKC; Hangul composition boundaries (`second > t_base`, LV only); stable canonical ordering; `quickCheck` never contradicts `normalize`; `max_output` is exact (`bytes.len > cap - len`).
- **Not covered by any foreign oracle** (kept in Open): `unaccent`'s lists (the review above is the only outside look), classification/title/casefold of the 4,815 code points new or changed in 17.0.0, `isNormalized` under `.replace` (an ill-formed stretch counts as neutral, so `isNormalized("\xFF", .nfc, .{ .invalid_utf8 = .replace })` is true although `normalize` would write U+FFFD; documented, left).
- LOW, left: `max_segment = 0` fails `"aé"` but not `"a"` (the ASCII shortcut never enters the segment); `unaccent` expands `Þ` to `TH` and `Æ`/`Œ` to `AE`/`OE` even before lowercase letters (`Œuvre` -> `OEuvre`, as Latin-ASCII).
